question: The anterior pituitary gland:

options.opa: It is part of the hypothalamus.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "part of the endocrine system" -> "receives regulatory hormones from the hypothalamus" -> "regulated hormonally" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "produces and secretes hormones" -> "communicates with the hypothalamus" -> "not formed by neurons" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "secretes hormones like ACTH, TSH, LH, FSH" -> "does not release ADH and oxytocin" -> "ADH and oxytocin are released by the posterior pituitary" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "connected to the hypothalamus" -> "communicates with the neurohypophysis" -> "via the infundibulum" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "produces hormones" -> "not formed by neurons" -> "formed by glandular tissue" -> 90%
analysis: The anterior pituitary gland is not part of the hypothalamus; it is a separate gland that is regulated hormonally by releasing and inhibiting hormones from the hypothalamus. It does not communicate with the neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) in the same way that the posterior pituitary releases ADH and oxytocin, which are produced in the hypothalamus. The anterior pituitary is formed from epithelial tissue, not neurons.
